evidence: REVIEWED — 3 findings, all in this ticket's own code, all fixed and re-verified. Full write-up at .autodev/evidence/T-2/review.md. (1) SECURITY, confirmed exploit not theory: the SPA fallback did 'dist / full_path' with no containment check, so curl --path-as-is on /../../.env returned 200 with bytes sha256-identical to the real .env carrying non-empty TMDB_API_KEY and PEXELS_API_KEY. Browsers normalise '..' so every browser test passed; non-browser clients do not. Loopback-only and nothing left the machine, so no rotation needed. Fixed by resolving the candidate and requiring dist_root containment (dist_root resolved once, so symlinks cannot widen it); re-tested 5 traversal payloads, all now return the SPA shell, while hashed CSS, /api/health and / are unaffected. (2) bootstrap() leaked a connection per call because 'with sqlite3.connect()' manages the transaction, not the connection; fixed with try/finally close, re-verified by counting /proc/self/fd across 50 bootstraps — 4 to 4, zero leaked. (3) WAL sidecars (-wal/-shm) hold uncheckpointed committed rows but were protected only by the data/ rule, so a relocated MEDIA_LIST_DB would thin the privacy boundary; added explicit ignores, re-verified with git check-ignore. Three further items considered and deliberately left with reasons recorded: per-call connections, import-time bootstrap, and start.sh's grep/cut .env read.
